Changelog

Sourced from astro's changelog.

6.4.8

Patch Changes

  • #17109 27c80ea Thanks @​ematipico! - Harden the limits on the number of decoding on the URL.

6.4.7

Patch Changes

  • #17035 197e50e Thanks @​astrobot-houston! - Fixes getRelativeLocaleUrl, getAbsoluteLocaleUrl, and getAbsoluteLocaleUrlList to strip trailing slashes when trailingSlash: 'never' is configured

  • #16967 3719765 Thanks @​astrobot-houston! - Fixes double URL-encoded paths returning 400 Bad Request on on-demand routes

    Previously, any URL containing a double-encoded character (like %255B, which is [ encoded twice) was unconditionally rejected with a 400 Bad Request before middleware or route handlers could run. This broke embedded tools like Sanity Studio whose client-side router legitimately produces double-encoded URLs.

    The fix replaces the rejection approach with iterative decoding — multi-level percent-encoding is now fully resolved to its canonical form before being passed to middleware and route matching. This preserves the security fix for CVE-2025-66202 (middleware authorization bypass via double encoding) because middleware now always sees the fully decoded path, making bypass impossible. For example, /api/%2561dmin is decoded to /api/admin, which middleware can correctly block.

  • #17066 2f4d92a Thanks @​matthewp! - Fixes prerendered redirect targets being incorrectly bundled into the SSR function in hybrid mode, causing massive bundle size inflation

  • #16882 621beb7 Thanks @​jettwayio! - fix(render): honour compressHTML when joining head elements

  • #16892 8d753b0 Thanks @​astrobot-houston! - Fixes custom elements in MDX having their children's slot attribute stripped by the JSX runtime

    When custom elements (tags with hyphens like <my-element>) are used in MDX files, the slot HTML attribute on their children is now correctly preserved. Previously, the shared JSX runtime would treat slot as an Astro slot assignment and remove it from the output, breaking Shadow DOM named slot distribution for web components.

  • #16957 544ee76 Thanks @​thelazylamaGit! - Fixes stale inline CSS in server-rendered HTML after CSS file edits during dev

    When editing a CSS file (.css, .scss, etc.) during development, the inline <style> tags in server-rendered HTML would retain old CSS content instead of updating. This caused a brief flash of old CSS (FOUC) on fresh page loads before Vite's client-side HMR corrected the styles.

    The fix ensures that Astro's per-route dev CSS virtual modules are invalidated in both the SSR module graph and the module runner's evaluation cache when a style file changes, so the next page render picks up the fresh CSS.

  • #17044 2220d22 Thanks @​astrobot-houston! - Fixes CSS from client:only islands leaking to unrelated pages when Rollup bundles non-CSS-importing modules into the same chunk as CSS-importing modules

  • #17040 7c4763d Thanks @​astrobot-houston! - Fixes HMR not triggering for files inside the src/middleware/ directory during dev

  • #16672 52fc862 Thanks @​martinheidegger! - Fixes support for numeric IDs in YAML frontmatter when using content collection references

snapshot_payload.body:
The vulnerability was in the `ping_host` function which used `os.popen(command)` to execute a shell command constructed with user input. This is vulnerable to CWE-78 (OS Command Injection) because the host parameter could contain shell metacharacters that get interpreted by the shell.

The fix replaces `os.popen()` with `subprocess.run()` and passes the command as a list of arguments instead of a single shell string. This prevents shell interpretation of the input, eliminating the command injection risk. The command is now structured as `["ping", "-c", "1", host]`, where each argument is passed separately to the ping process, making it safe from shell injection attacks.

The `subprocess.run()` call also uses `capture_output=True` and `text=True` to maintain the same behavior of returning stdout as a string, while properly handling the command execution without shell interpretation.

snapshot_payload.body: ## Production verification / hardening **Status: READY WITH MANUAL E2E REQUIRED** Do not treat this as verified Google Meet-like A/V until two authenticated users complete the HTTPS LiveKit checklist below. Code inspection and automated tests passed; live camera/microphone exchange was **not** executed in this environment. Architecture preserved: Flutter → Flask REST/Socket.IO → PostgreSQL; video → LiveKit Cloud; AI → existing STT/Whisper + `meeting_sessions` summary. gunicorn remains `-w 1`. --- ### 1. What was already correct - Project/team chat and DMs use real numeric room IDs. `POST /api/chat/direct` find-or-creates 1:1 rooms; `direct_pair_key` (`min:max`) prevents duplicate DMs. - Socket.IO `join_chat` / `send_message` return acknowledgements and emit `error`; REST send remains the fallback; message `idempotency_key` is used. - Meetings are PostgreSQL rows with UUID `public_id`, `provider_room = teamify_{uuid}`, unique `(meeting_id, user_id)` participants. - Flask mints LiveKit JWTs only after Teamify membership checks. Identity is `str(user_id)`, room is `provider_room`. Host gets `roomAdmin`/`roomCreate`. TTL 7200s. Missing LiveKit config returns **503** (no fake join). - Flutter uses `livekit_client` with `joinToken.url` + `joinToken.token` (not the Teamify JWT). Preview uses real `LocalVideoTrack.createCameraTrack()`. - Chat and DMs start meetings via `POST /api/meetings` with integer `chat_room_id`. Invitations use in-app notifications with `meeting:{uuid}` in the body. Join route `/meeting/join/` exists; Firebase and Netlify SPA rewrites send unknown paths to `index.html`. - Duplicate AppConfig is resolved (`lib/core/config/app_config.dart` + re-export). `API_BASE_URL` defaults to the Render backend. No `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` in Flutter source. - REST CORS is an explicit origin list (not `*`). `.env` is gitignored. Procfile: `gunicorn -w 1` + `GeventWebSocketWorker`. Health: `GET /api/health`. - Host-only end was already enforced for members who are not the host (403). Auth is required on all meeting endpoints. ### 2. What was actually broken - **Host end did not close the LiveKit room.** PostgreSQL status became `ended`, but remotes stayed in media until they disconnected themselves. The live UI only showed “Disconnected”. - **Wrong transcript could attach to a meeting.** GET meeting and `end_meeting` fell back to *any* `MeetingSession` for the chat room. `start_meeting_session` could reuse another meeting’s active session if it was <300s old. - **Unauthorized token/end leaked meeting existence.** Outsiders got 403 (“not allowed” / “only the host”) instead of 404. - **Race: two live meetings for one chat room.** Application reuse existed, but there was no unique partial index, and concurrent creates could insert two live rows (two LiveKit rooms). - **Startup schema patches added columns but not unique indexes** (`direct_pair_key`, `idempotency_key`). - **Production STT defaulted to `http://localhost:8000`.** Copying `.env.example` onto Render would post audio to loopback. - **Camera/mic publish failures aborted the whole LiveKit connect.** Permission errors were not isolated. - **Ended-meeting summary from the list** used `meeting.session`, which the list API does not include. ### 3. What was fixed - Host end commits Teamify state, then calls LiveKit RoomService `DeleteRoom` (best-effort; 404 treated as already gone). Client leaves the screen on `RoomDisconnectedEvent`. - Sessions are linked only by `meeting_id`. Starting a session for a live meeting creates/reuses that meeting’s session and closes orphan active sessions for the same room without stealing their transcript. - Unauthorized token/leave/end: **404** if the caller cannot access the meeting. Non-host members still get **403** on end. - Partial unique index `uq_meetings_one_live_per_room` on `(chat_room_id) WHERE status = 'live'`, plus IntegrityError reuse. Duplicate live rows are ended (keeping newest) before the index is created. - Runtime patches also create unique indexes for live meetings, message idempotency, and `direct_pair_key`. - `FLASK_ENV=production` ignores localhost / 127.0.0.1 / 0.0.0.0 `STT_SERVICE_URL` and transcribe returns 503 instead of hanging on loopback. - Camera and microphone are published separately after connect; failures show a snackbar and leave the user in the meeting without that track. - Preview blocks non-HTTPS web (except localhost). Ended meetings from the list fetch GET details so the linked session can load. ### 4. Exact files changed (hardening commit) - `teamify_flask_backend/services/livekit_token_service.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/services/meeting_service.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/routes/meetings.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/routes/chat.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/routes/ai.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/config.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/app.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/models/meeting.py` - `teamify_flask_backend/.env.example` - `teamify_flask_backend/tests/test_direct_chat_and_meetings.py` - `teamify_flutter/lib/screens/meeting/live_meeting_screen.dart` - `teamify_flutter/lib/screens/meeting/meeting_preview_screen.dart` - `teamify_flutter/lib/screens/meeting/meetings_list_screen.dart` ### 5. Database migrations changed/added - Existing (unchanged): `n4o5p6q7r8s9_add_meetings_and_direct_pair.py` — meetings table, participants, `direct_pair_key`, `meeting_sessions.meeting_id`, message idempotency. - **Added:** `o5p6q7r8s9t0_harden_meeting_constraints.py` — ends duplicate live meetings (keeps newest per room), then creates: - `uq_meetings_one_live_per_room` (partial unique) - `uq_msg_idempotency` if missing - `uq_chat_rooms_direct_pair_key` if missing - Non-destructive. Startup patches in `app.py` apply the same indexes if Alembic has not run. ### 6. Environment variables required **Render (Flask)** | Variable | Notes | |---|---| | `DATABASE_URL` | PostgreSQL | | `JWT_SECRET_KEY` | Required in production | | `FLASK_ENV=production` | Enables secure cookies / CSRF and STT loopback guard | | `LIVEKIT_URL` | Public URL (`wss://…livekit.cloud` or `https://…`). **Not a secret.** | | `LIVEKIT_API_KEY` | Server only | | `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` | Server only — never in Flutter | | `CORS_ORIGINS` | Comma-separated production web origins | | `STT_SERVICE_URL` | Optional. Must be a reachable Whisper URL if server STT is required. Do **not** set localhost in production. | | `AI_ENABLE_LOCAL_MODELS` | `false` recommended on Render free/512MB | **Flutter web build (optional dart-defines)** - `API_BASE_URL` (defaults to `https://teamify-backend-5hq0.onrender.com`) - `LIVEKIT_URL` is optional; the join API returns the URL. Never pass `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET`. ### 7. Security findings | Finding | Severity | Status | |---|---|---| | LiveKit secret never in Flutter source or web release build (`grep` of `build/web` found no `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` / `LIVEKIT_API_KEY`) | — | OK | | No `.env` committed | — | OK | | Meeting UUID does not bypass membership | High | Fixed (token 404) | | Outsider `POST .../end` enumerated meetings | Medium | Fixed (404 if no access) | | Transcript/session from another meeting on same room | High | Fixed | | REST CORS is explicit; Socket.IO still `cors_allowed_origins="*"` (needed for engine.io; REST `/api/*` is not wildcard) | Low | Accepted / unchanged | | LiveKit participant JWT `iss` is the API **key** (standard LiveKit). snapshot_payload.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `sql.listen()` and `sql.notify()` for PostgreSQL (`LISTEN`/`NOTIFY`). Originally #29710 by @versecafe; this is a from-scratch rewrite of both the native and the JS side, rebased onto current main (design and numbers below, the earlier implementation is referred to as v1).

```ts
import { sql } from "bun";

const subscription = await sql.listen("orders", payload => {
  console.log("new order", JSON.parse(payload));
});

await sql.notify("orders", JSON.stringify({ id: 42 }));
await subscription.unlisten();

// or scoped:
await using subscription = await sql.listen("orders", handleOrder);
```

- `listen(channel, onnotify, onlisten?)` resolves once the server acknowledged the `LISTEN`, with a `ListenSubscription` (`channel`, `unlisten()`, `Symbol.asyncDispose`) that removes exactly the registration that call made. Every call is its own registration; several on one channel share one server-side `LISTEN`. `onlisten()` runs on the acknowledgement and again after every reconnect (the place to catch up on missed notifications). Shape per the review discussion below; there is no `sql.unlisten()` and no pid/secret exposure.
- `notify(channel, payload?)` is `SELECT pg_notify($1, $2)` on the handle it is called on, so `tx.notify()` is delivered on commit and dropped on rollback. Reserved and transaction handles have both methods.
- All subscriptions of a client share one dedicated connection, opened by the first `listen()` and closed when the last subscription is removed; while anything is subscribed it keeps the process alive (#32127). If it drops, it reconnects with jittered exponential backoff (250ms to 32s) and re-subscribes every channel. `sql.close()` tears it down, including mid-handshake.
- Channel names are quoted as identifiers and limited to PostgreSQL's 63 identifier bytes; a throwing callback is reported as an uncaught exception. Non-Postgres adapters reject with "PostgreSQL only".

### Design

Hot path (one `NotificationResponse`), native side in `PostgresSQLConnection.rs`:

1. `NotificationResponse::decode` yields the channel and payload as slices into the read buffer (`string_within`), nothing is copied. v1 copied both into `Vec`s.
2. The channel slice is looked up in a small per-connection table of interned `JSString`s (`Strong`, at most 256 entries), so after the first notification on a channel the channel name costs a scan of that table and no allocation. v1 created a new string every time.
3. The payload becomes one `JSString` (`create_utf8_for_js`, the string owns the only copy).
4. The JS callback is invoked synchronously with `run_callback`, the same way query results are delivered; exceptions surface as uncaught. v1 queued a microtask per notification.

`ref()` on a connection now sets `KEEP_ALIVE_REQUESTED` so the idle-unref at the end of `on_data` leaves the listen connection ref'd.

JS side (`src/js/internal/sql/postgres.ts`): one `ListenConnection` per adapter holding a `Map<channel, Channel>` plus the connection, sweep timer and backoff fields; a `ListenSubscription` only remembers its channel and callbacks and hands them back on `unlisten()`. Dispatch is `Map.get` followed by a direct call (a lone listener is stored as the bare function; several are stored in an array that is replaced rather than mutated, so `listen()`/`unlisten()` from inside a callback cannot disturb the dispatch in progress). A `Channel` entry's identity scopes its `LISTEN` round trip: removing the last registration deletes the entry synchronously, and anything resuming after an await compares its entry against the map, which removes the re-add / unlisten-during-ack races v1 needed separate bookkeeping for. There is exactly one repair mechanism: a connection drop, connect failure or rejected `LISTEN` nulls the affected entries' `ready` promise and arms `#scheduleSweep()`, which re-issues `LISTEN` for those entries. v1 kept five channel-keyed maps and sets (listeners, onlisten callbacks, in-flight round trips, channels registered on the current connection, failure counters) consistent by hand for the same job.

### Numbers

Both builds are release builds of this branch's base with the respective implementation applied, measured against a scripted backend in a separate process that writes pre-built frames (it sustains over 10M frames/s into a sink, so the client is what is measured). 4 channels, medians of 5 runs of 1M notifications, two passes each.

| payload | v1 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32 bytes | 3.65M to 4.10M notifications/s (244 to 274 ns each) | 4.91M to 5.37M notifications/s (186 to 204 ns each) |
| 256 bytes | 2.74M to 2.83M/s | 2.86M to 2.89M/s (both bounded by socket reads on this machine) |

JS heap objects per notification (`bun:jsc` `heapStats()` delta across a blast with no collection in between): v1 allocated 2 strings plus a Set iterator (until the JIT elides it), this PR allocates the 1 payload string. Native allocations per notification went from two `Vec`s plus two string buffers plus a microtask entry to one string buffer.

### How did you verify your code works?

`test/js/sql/postgres-listen-notify.test.ts`, 56 tests:

- 44 run against a scripted backend in the test process (which can hold a `LISTEN` ack, fail one, or drop the connection on demand) or in a subprocess: routing and ordering, thousands of notifications in one read, UTF-8 and quoting, the 63-byte limit, listeners added or removed from inside a callback, shared round trips, the same callback registered twice being two subscriptions, `onlisten` timing, `unlisten()` and `await using` removing exactly their own registration (idempotent, and a no-op on a handle that outlived `close()`), a re-listen while the UNLISTEN is in flight, reconnect (re-subscribe, an unlistened subscription's `onlisten` no longer firing, retry with warning, cancelled by unlistening, a shared listen() whose LISTEN is rejected still repairing the other listeners), `close()` during a round trip, during the handshake and in the same tick as a listen() on the live connection, argument validation on Postgres and SQLite, `notify()` going through the pool, and in a subprocess: the subscription keeping the process alive (also across the backoff), `close()` letting it exit, throwing `onnotify` and `onlisten` callbacks reaching `uncaughtException` without affecting the other listeners, and an RSS check over 2 x 24 MiB of payloads that fails when one string per notification is leaked (verified by injecting that leak).
- 12 run against the docker postgres: payload round trips including empty and omitted payloads, commit/rollback delivery, and the ten LISTEN/NOTIFY tests of postgres.js's own suite ported under their original names (weird and upper-case channel names, double listen, unlisten variants, reconnect after the listening backend is terminated), with their delays replaced by waiting for the deliveries. These also pass against a local PostgreSQL 17.

All of them fail on main (`sql.listen is not a function`).

Fixes #18214
Fixes #32127

## Summary

Adds an **arbitrary-file lane** to agentdraft so `agentdraft file <path>` uploads any local
file (screenshot, recording, log, PDF, zip, build artifact) and returns a stable public URL
— our in-house replacement for third-party file hosts. Reuses the existing workers, R2
bucket, D1, auth, and CLI (Option A: shared origin).

Documents already worked via `agentdraft upload` (HTML/Markdown, validated + rendered).
This adds the binary lane alongside it, served as-is.

## Security model (the core of this change)

Arbitrary files share the content origin with rendered documents, so a naively-served file
could execute as a page there. The gate that prevents it:

- **Attachment by default.** Every file serves `Content-Disposition: attachment` UNLESS its
  MIME is on a strict inline allowlist (`image/png|jpeg|gif|webp|avif`, `video/mp4|webm`,
  `audio/mpeg|mp4`, `text/plain`, `application/pdf`).
- **`text/html` and `image/svg+xml` are never inline** — the two script-carrying types.
- **`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` always**, so a file lying about its type can't be
  reinterpreted as markup.
- Serve response is `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `noindex`, `CORP: same-origin`.
- The allowlist is duplicated in both workers (they don't share a module) with a comment
  keeping them in sync, and is asserted by unit tests.

## What's included

- **DB:** `0005_files.sql` — `files` table (unversioned; soft-delete + disable columns).
- **API worker:** `POST /api/files` (streams the raw body straight to R2, never buffered;
  100 MB cap; idempotency-key dedupe), `GET /api/files` (list, read scope),
  `POST /api/files/:id/disable` (takedown, ownership in the query).
- **Content worker:** `GET /f/:id` — attachment-default serve with the inline allowlist,
  nosniff, hard-immutable cache, `304` revalidation, and `Range`/`206` for media seeking.
- **CLI:** `agentdraft file <path>` with `--content-type` / `--idempotency-key`, streaming
  upload with no client timeout, 100 MB local pre-check.
- **Dashboard:** a Files list page (name/type/size/date/link + disable) and a nav link.
- **Skill:** `agentdraft-file-upload` replacing the external file-host skill.
- **Docs:** `api.md` + `cli.md` updated.

## What was tested (real prod, deployed workers)

```
PNG  → content-disposition: inline; content-type: image/png; nosniff        ✓
LOG  → inline; text/plain                                                    ✓
MP4  → inline; video/mp4; accept-ranges: bytes                              ✓
HTML → content-disposition: ATTACHMENT; nosniff   (must not serve inline)    ✓
SVG  → content-disposition: ATTACHMENT; nosniff   (must not serve inline)    ✓
Range GET bytes=0-99  → 206, content-range: bytes 0-99/2233, 100 bytes       ✓
Range GET bytes=-50   → 206, 50 bytes                                        ✓
Range GET malformed   → 416                                                  ✓
Integrity: served sha256 == source sha256                                    ✓
```

snapshot_payload.body:
Rewrites CanteenX end to end. The previous build demoed well but had several
paths that could not work in production, and a few that were actively unsafe.

## Security fixes

- **Free orders.** `POST /api/payment/verify` had no auth, and because every seeded merchant carried the literal key `rzp_test_YOUR_KEY_ID`, the gateway selection fell through to a mock that accepted any payload and returned `"captured"`. Anyone with curl could mark an order paid. Payments now verify an HMAC signature, re-confirm status and amount with Razorpay, and treat a signed idempotent webhook as the authoritative confirmation.
- **`markOrderPaid` is gone.** It let a customer flip their own order to paid with no payment involved.
- **Authorization.** Only 5 of 23 queries carried any policy; anonymous callers could read other users' carts, orders, payment history, complaints, and per-canteen revenue. Every field now declares a policy, and a test fails the build if one is ever added without it.
- Committed fallback secrets removed; config fails fast instead. Razorpay secrets no longer stored as plaintext columns. CSRF double-submit added, refresh-token rotation with reuse detection implemented (the previous refresh cookie was issued and never read, so every session died silently after 15 minutes).

## Correctness fixes

- **Money is integer paise**, not `Float`.
- **Stock is transactional** — reserved at checkout via a conditional UPDATE with a rowcount check, and returned on cancellation. Previously it was decremented and never restored, so every abandoned checkout leaked inventory permanently.
- **Order status is an enum with a transition table**; it was unvalidated free text.
- **One schema source of truth.** `create_all()` at import time plus three competing migration systems replaced with a single Alembic baseline. `alembic check` runs in CI. The `script.py.mako` template had its `${upgrades}` placeholder replaced with `pass`, so every autogenerated migration came out empty — that is why the old ones were hand-written and drifted.
- Several core mutations (`create_canteen`, `create_menu_item`, `create_complaint`, `register_user`) raised on **every** call by assigning to read-only camelCase property shims. That whole layer is deleted.

## Bugs found by testing this build

- **WebSocket handshake** died with a `TypeError` — FastAPI injects `websocket`, not `request`. No subscription had ever connected.
- **Connection-pool exhaustion.** A dependency resolved on a WS route is held for the whole connection, so each subscription pinned a pooled DB connection. Hit live: the entire API started returning `QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 2 reached`.
- **A race in `user()`** set its memoisation flag before awaiting the query, so a second concurrent subscription read `None` and rejected a valid user on timing alone.
- **Every upload would have failed in production.** Filenames were generated as `menu/<uuid>.webp`, and the storage server rejects any name containing a slash. Also fixed: the upload path, the separate read host, and taking the path from the response (its `url` field points at the wrong domain).
- `PaymentsDisabledError` was swallowed by a broad `except` and reported as a generic payment failure.

## Frontend

Rewritten: ~2,200 lines of unreachable code removed, TypeScript strict on, GraphQL types generated rather than hand-maintained, Tailwind v4, Apollo rebuilt with CSRF, 401-refresh-retry, and a `graphql-ws` split. The cart existed in three incompatible places at once and is now server-only. Promotions, bulk orders, vendor settings, inventory and pre-order were pure `useState` mockups and now persist. New design system on the ADK DEV brand violet with working light/dark. Both consoles get the mobile navigation they never had.

## Verification

- 32 backend tests, including regression tests for each bug above
- 39-check end-to-end smoke script
- Order lifecycle, wallet payment, live subscription updates, and image upload all confirmed in Chrome
- ruff / tsc / eslint clean; `vite build` succeeds; `alembic check` reports no drift

## Not done

Responsive behaviour at 375/768/1440 is **not** verified in a browser, and Lighthouse has not been run. The work is in (mobile drawers, table scroll containers, focus rings, `aria-live`, reduced-motion) but unverified.

Setup, environment variables, and deployment are documented in `DEVDOC.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary

Close CodeQL **alert #595** (java/ldap-injection, critical) on `system/src/main/java/com/percussion/security/PSJndiGroupProvider.java:200` — the only open LDAP-injection Critical+High alert on `main` as of 2026-08-12.

Includes the prerequisite `pom.xml` unbreak from PR #31 (same branch) so the PR compiles under `./mvn-env.sh validate`.

## Vulnerability

`PSJndiUtils.getFilterString` builds an LDAP search filter from user-supplied values without escaping RFC 4515 reserved characters. An attacker who controls a filter argument can break out of the parenthesised comparison:

```
filter = "*)(uid=*"   // attacker input
// before fix: (cn=*)(uid=*)
// after fix:  (cn=\2a\29\28uid=\2a)
```

Result: a query meant to be `cn=foo` becomes `(|(cn=*)(uid=*))`, exposing every entry in the directory.

## Fix

- `PSJndiUtils.getFilterString`: escape each user filter value via a new `escapeLdapFilterValue` helper before composing the LDAP search filter.
- `PSJndiUtils.escapeLdapFilterValue` (package-private): hex-escapes RFC 4515 reserved chars (\`, `(`, `)`, NUL) and UTF-8 multi-byte sequences. The `*` wildcard is **preserved** because `processFilter` maps the documented `%` input syntax to `*` and the public contract treats `*` as a wildcard.
- `PSJndiUtilsLdapInjectionTest` (JUnit 4, 9 tests): reserved-char escape, wildcard preservation, ASCII passthrough, UTF-8 byte-by-byte escape, null/empty inputs, and the end-to-end `*)(uid=*` injection vector.

## Pattern source

Backported from the 004 spec branch (PR #1345 `e8489b698a` — same CodeQL rule, same fix family).

## Verification

```bash
./mvn-env.sh -pl system test -Dtest=PSJndiUtilsLdapInjectionTest
# => Tests run: 9, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0

./mvn-env.sh -pl system spotless:apply && ./mvn-env.sh -pl system spotless:check
# => BUILD SUCCESS

./mvn-env.sh validate
# => BUILD SUCCESS (after the pom.xml fix on this branch)
```

Regression check (local, not committed): reverting the `escapeLdapFilterValue` call inside `getFilterString` makes `getFilterStringEscapesUserInputFromInjection` fail with the unescaped `*)(uid=*` payload.

## Files

- `system/src/main/java/com/percussion/security/PSJndiUtils.java` (+46 lines: escape helper + 5-line getFilterString call)
- `system/Testing/src/com/percussion/security/PSJndiUtilsLdapInjectionTest.java` (new, 119 lines)
- `pom.xml` (+2 / -5: unbreak duplicated close tags — prerequisite for any build on `main`)
- `CHANGELOG.md` (Task 2 + build-fix entries)

## Notes

- No legacy component removed; `PSJndiUtils` stays in `system/` with public contract intact.
- No Maven dependency change; `*.version` properties untouched per the Java 8 stack constraint.
- Per AGENTS.md, `Version.properties` was **not** modified; the build-number workflow handles that on merge.

## 🔒 Security exhibit #0066: the server that trusted the request

**Rule:** never read price or status from the **request body** - the server owns them, keyed by id

### What it teaches
The request body is **input**, not state - every field is whatever the client chose to send (curl, a script, a modified page). Model-binding `Price`/`Status`/`Role`/`UserId` straight from it hands those decisions to the caller. The broken belief is "I validated the request, so it's safe": validation checks *shape* (types, ranges), never *authority* - `unitPrice: 0.01` and `status: "Paid"` are both perfectly valid. So a client prices its own order **and** marks it paid. Fix: accept only client-owned fields (which product, how many); derive money and status from the server's own source of truth, keyed by an id.

A hybrid of two declined validation-only candidates (client-supplied price + mass assignment), deliberately elementary but put on one screen where money and privilege break together.

### Deterministic reproduction
A catalog `{SKU-1: 49.99}` and a request `{ProductId: SKU-1, Quantity: 1, UnitPrice: 0.01, Status: "Paid"}`. Culture pinned invariant. Verified on .NET 10:
- `dotnet run Bad.cs` → `Charged 0.01 for 1 x SKU-1, status Paid`, then throws (charged 0.01 != catalog 49.99) (exit 134)
- `dotnet run Good.cs` → `Charged 49.99 for 1 x SKU-1, status Pending` (exit 0)

The mirror is two lines: `UnitPrice = req.UnitPrice` → `catalog[req.ProductId]`, and `Status = req.Status` → `"Pending"`.

### Notable README content
- **😈** the penny order is the *loud* version (reconciliation catches it); the quiet ones are `userId`/`tenantId` bound from the body (IDOR - read/write others' data) and a `isPaid`/`emailVerified` boolean that flips a workflow with no error. Money you can reconcile; ownership and status you often can't. Same wrong-price outcome as [0012-zero-priced-order](src/serialization/0012-zero-priced-order/), from the other direction.
- **🎓** validation ≠ authorization; the authenticated identity is server state (from the token, not the body); even "hidden" form fields are client-editable on the wire.
- **🔎** grep actions binding a DTO and assigning `Price`/`Total`/`Status`/`Role`/`UserId` from it; a domain entity used directly as `[FromBody]`.

### Housekeeping
- Curator's own exhibit (uncredited). Invented hybrid (not from the backlog); its two source framings were declined separately this session. Front page regenerated; `tools/check-links.cs` passes (66 exhibits, cross-link to #0012 resolves). Memory in a separate commit.

Two isolated commits so the forced mongoose bump can be reverted independently if needed:

1. **`3e6aefd`** — safe fixes via `npm audit fix` (no `--force`): body-parser (DoS, low), nanoid (infinite loop, high), on-headers/compression (header manipulation, low), postcss (arbitrary .map file disclosure, high). All transitive bumps within existing `package.json` ranges — package.json itself unchanged.
2. **`45f4d5c`** — forced fix via `npm audit fix --force`: mongoose `8.15.0` → `^8.24.3`, fixing:
   - [GHSA-wpg9-53fq-2r8h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wpg9-53fq-2r8h) — improper `$nor` sanitization in `sanitizeFilter`, NoSQL injection (high)
   - [GHSA-664h-wqgq-64gw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-664h-wqgq-64gw) — prototype pollution via `__proto__`-prefixed dotted path in update casting (high)

   `8.24.3` is outside the previously *exact-pinned* `8.15.0`, but still within the same major version (8.x).

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean after both commits.
- **No test suite exists in this repo** (no `test` script, no `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` files) — noted, not run.
- Grepped for `$nor`, `sanitizeFilter`, and dynamic dotted-path update keys — the exact patterns the two mongoose CVEs are in: none found. All `updateOne`/`updateMany`/`findOneAndUpdate` calls in this codebase use static, hardcoded field names, not user-controlled paths.
- Live behavioral proof anyway, since mongoose touches every data write: spun up a local in-memory MongoDB (`mongodb-memory-server`, installed with `--no-save`, not a persisted dependency), ran `db:bootstrap` against it, started the dev server pointed at it (so it's actually exercising the new `mongoose@8.24.3`, unlike testing against the still-on-old-version production site), and submitted a real booking:
  ```
  POST /api/bookings → 201
  ```

### undici vulnerable to cross-user information disclosure via shared cache whitespace bypass
[CVE-2026-9678](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9678) / [GHSA-pr7r-676h-xcf6](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-pr7r-676h-xcf6)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Undici's cache interceptor incorrectly classifies some responses as cacheable when the upstream `Cache-Control` header uses whitespace-padded qualified `private` or `no-cache` field names such as `private=" authorization"` or `no-cache="\tauthorization"`. The parser preserves the surrounding whitespace, so later comparisons against the literal `authorization` field name fail and the response is stored.

In shared-cache mode, this allows a response containing one user's authenticated data to be served from cache to a subsequent caller, including an unauthenticated caller, when both requests resolve to the same cache key.

Affected applications are those that explicitly enable the cache interceptor (`interceptors.cache()`) in shared mode, forward `Authorization` headers upstream, and receive cacheable responses with non-canonical qualified `private` or `no-cache` directives.

##### Patches

Upgrade to undici v7.28.0 or v8.5.0.

##### Workarounds

If upgrade is not immediately possible, disable shared-cache mode for traffic that includes `Authorization` headers, avoid caching responses to authenticated requests, or add `Vary: Authorization` upstream.

### undici vulnerable to cross-user information disclosure and parse-time crash via degenerate private cache directives
[CVE-2026-13697](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-13697) / [GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

Two issues in undici's cache interceptor, both fixed by the same patch on `lib/util/cache.js`:

1. **Shared-cache disclosure:** Responses with malformed qualified `Cache-Control: private` directives such as `private=""` or `private=","` can be incorrectly stored in the default shared cache, then served to a later caller with the same cache key.
2. **Parse-time crash:** Mixed unqualified-and-qualified `private` directives in the same header (such as `public, max-age=60, private, private="hdr"`) cause an uncaught `TypeError` in the cache-control parser, terminating the request.

##### Impact

##### Shared-cache disclosure

Applications using `interceptors.cache()` in shared mode may cache a user-specific response and serve it to a later caller with the same cache key. This can disclose private response bodies and headers, including `Set-Cookie`.

Required conditions:

- the cache interceptor is enabled in shared mode, including the default configuration;
- an upstream returns a malformed directive such as `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, private=""`;
- another request later matches the same cache key, without a separating `Vary` header.

##### Parse-time crash

Applications using `interceptors.cache()` against an upstream that returns a `Cache-Control` header combining unqualified `private` with qualified `private="..."` see an uncaught `TypeError: output.private.concat is not a function` during response handling. The request rejects; depending on the consumer's error handling, the process may exit.

##### Details

`private=""` is parsed as `{ private: [''] }`. The shared-cache guard only rejects `private === true`, so the response can be stored. When served from cache, the previous user's body and headers may be returned to a different user.

For the crash variant, an unqualified `private` directive sets `output.private = true`, then a subsequent qualified `private="hdr"` directive attempts `output.private.concat(['hdr'])`, which throws because boolean has no `concat` method.

The patch routes the qualified-directive path through a shared helper that normalizes empty-after-trim arrays to `true` and preserves existing `true` values, closing both vectors.

##### Patches

Upgrade to `undici` 7.29.0 or 8.9.0. Both releases fix the qualified `private` directive handling that caused the shared-cache storage and the parser crash.

##### Workarounds

Until patched, avoid shared `interceptors.cache()` for user-specific responses, use `type: 'private'`, or disable caching for affected origins.

##### Credit

Disclosure variant reported by @​h0rk1p via HackerOne report [#​3817497](https://hackerone.com/reports/3817497).

### undici vulnerable to downstream response desynchronization via retry interceptor
[CVE-2026-16728](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-16728) / [GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524)

<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Undici's `interceptors.retry()` can deliver a response whose body length does not match the `Content-Length` header exposed to the application after a retry or resume of a partial response. Applications that use `interceptors.retry()` and forward upstream response headers and bodies downstream, for example proxy or gateway applications, may emit an invalid HTTP response with a stale `Content-Length` header. This can lead to downstream response desynchronization, connection hangs, or response corruption in clients or intermediaries that rely on the forwarded framing metadata.

A malicious or faulty upstream can respond to a range request with a `206 Partial Content` response such as:

The bug requires `interceptors.retry()` to be enabled, an upstream that returns a partial response with a mismatched framing header, and a downstream forwarder that does not remove or recalculate `Content-Length`.

##### Patches

Patched in undici v6.28.0, v7.29.0, and v8.9.0. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later.

##### Workarounds

- Disable `interceptors.retry()` for untrusted upstreams.
- Remove or recalculate `Content-Length` before forwarding a response body assembled or transformed by Undici.

### undici vulnerable to CRLF Injection via blob-like body 'type' property
[CVE-2026-15157](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15157) / [GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

When an application passes a duck-typed blob-like body to undici's HTTP/1.1 dispatcher (via `request()`, `stream()`, `pipeline()`, or `dispatch()`) with a `.type` derived from untrusted input, an attacker can inject CRLF sequences (`\r\n`) to append arbitrary HTTP headers and potentially smuggle a second request past the upstream.

The vulnerable branch in `lib/dispatcher/client-h1.js` pushes `body.type` directly into the outgoing headers with no validation, while every other header path in undici goes through `isValidHeaderValue()`:

```javascript
} else if (util.isBlobLike(body) && request.contentType == null && body.type) {
  headers.push('content-type', body.type)  // bypasses isValidHeaderValue()
}
```

The bug requires a hand-rolled duck-typed blob object or a Blob subclass with a controlled `.type`. Native `Blob` is safe because its constructor strips CRLF from `.type`. `fetch()` is unaffected because it validates via the `Headers` class. Ecosystem consumers that build duck-typed blob shapes from user input include `form-data-encoder`, `formdata-polyfill`, and `formdata-node`.

Same defect class as `CVE-2022-35948` (explicit `content-type` sink, fixed in undici 5.8.2) and `CVE-2026-1527` (`upgrade` option sink, fixed in 6.24.0 / 7.24.0), both closed by adding `isValidHeaderValue()` on their respective sinks. This branch was missed.

##### Patches

Patched in undici v6.28.0, v7.29.0, and v8.9.0. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later.

##### Workarounds

- Set an explicit, validated `content-type` header on the request options (skips the vulnerable branch).
- Use a native `Blob` (or `fetch-blob`) instead of a hand-rolled duck-typed object.
- Reject control characters in the MIME type before assigning it to `.type`.
- Use `fetch()` instead of the non-`fetch` APIs.

After parsing a `Set-Cookie` header, validate that the resulting `sameSite` attribute is one of `'Strict'`, `'Lax'`, or `'None'` (exact, case-insensitive) before forwarding or relying on it.

<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Undici's cache interceptor incorrectly classifies some responses as cacheable when the upstream `Cache-Control` header uses whitespace-padded qualified `private` or `no-cache` field names such as `private=" authorization"` or `no-cache="\tauthorization"`. Affected applications are those that explicitly enable the cache interceptor (`interceptors.cache()`) in shared mode, forward `Authorization` headers upstream, and receive cacheable responses with non-canonical qualified `private` or `no-cache` directives.

##### Patches

Upgrade to undici v7.28.0 or v8.5.0.

##### Workarounds

If upgrade is not immediately possible, disable shared-cache mode for traffic that includes `Authorization` headers, avoid caching responses to authenticated requests, or add `Vary: Authorization` upstream.

### undici vulnerable to cross-user information disclosure and parse-time crash via degenerate private cache directives
[CVE-2026-13697](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-13697) / [GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

Two issues in undici's cache interceptor, both fixed by the same patch on `lib/util/cache.js`:

1. **Shared-cache disclosure:** Responses with malformed qualified `Cache-Control: private` directives such as `private=""` or `private=","` can be incorrectly stored in the default shared cache, then served to a later caller with the same cache key.
2. **Parse-time crash:** Mixed unqualified-and-qualified `private` directives in the same header (such as `public, max-age=60, private, private="hdr"`) cause an uncaught `TypeError` in the cache-control parser, terminating the request.

##### Impact

##### Shared-cache disclosure

Applications using `interceptors.cache()` in shared mode may cache a user-specific response and serve it to a later caller with the same cache key. This can disclose private response bodies and headers, including `Set-Cookie`.

Required conditions:

- the cache interceptor is enabled in shared mode, including the default configuration;
- an upstream returns a malformed directive such as `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, private=""`;
- another request later matches the same cache key, without a separating `Vary` header.

##### Parse-time crash

Applications using `interceptors.cache()` against an upstream that returns a `Cache-Control` header combining unqualified `private` with qualified `private="..."` see an uncaught `TypeError: output.private.concat is not a function` during response handling. The request rejects; depending on the consumer's error handling, the process may exit.

##### Details

`private=""` is parsed as `{ private: [''] }`. The shared-cache guard only rejects `private === true`, so the response can be stored. When served from cache, the previous user's body and headers may be returned to a different user.

For the crash variant, an unqualified `private` directive sets `output.private = true`, then a subsequent qualified `private="hdr"` directive attempts `output.private.concat(['hdr'])`, which throws because boolean has no `concat` method.

The patch routes the qualified-directive path through a shared helper that normalizes empty-after-trim arrays to `true` and preserves existing `true` values, closing both vectors.

##### Patches

Upgrade to `undici` 7.29.0 or 8.9.0. Both releases fix the qualified `private` directive handling that caused the shared-cache storage and the parser crash.

##### Workarounds

Until patched, avoid shared `interceptors.cache()` for user-specific responses, use `type: 'private'`, or disable caching for affected origins.

##### Credit

Disclosure variant reported by @​h0rk1p via HackerOne report [#​3817497](https://hackerone.com/reports/3817497).

##### Patches

Patched in undici v6.28.0, v7.29.0, and v8.9.0. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later.

snapshot_payload.body:
`assertSafeSavePath` promised "no writing outside sensible roots, **no path traversal**" and delivered only the first half. It resolved with `resolve(p)` — which collapses `..` but knows nothing about symlinks — then compared prefixes. A link *inside* an allowed root passed, and Notes.app's AppleScript `save` followed it out.

**Reproduced before any code was written:**

```
~/.probe-XXXX/escape -> /etc
assertSafeSavePath("~/.probe-XXXX/escape/hosts")
  -> ALLOWED, returned /Users/rob/.probe-XXXX/escape/hosts
```

## The fix

The destination file normally does not exist yet, so the whole path cannot simply be realpath'd. Instead: canonicalize the deepest **existing** ancestor (walked with `lstat`, so a dangling or looping link still counts as existing), check it against the canonicalized roots, then reassemble and re-check the full destination. A destination that already exists as a symlink is refused rather than followed.

Canonicalization uses `fs.realpathSync.native`, not the JS `realpathSync` — the latter preserves the caller's casing and is defeated on case-insensitive APFS by respelling a segment. Same class of bug as apple-mail-mcp 2.10.29. The roots go through the same call, which is what keeps `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` and `/var/folders` → `/private/var/folders` working for callers that pass an already-resolved real path.

`ensureParentDir` now validates **before** `mkdirSync(recursive)`. `mkdir -p` builds directories *through* a symlink, so validate-after-mkdir plants the very escape the check exists to prevent. The sole call site already validated first; this makes it a property of the function rather than of its callers.

## Follow-ups from adversarial review (same PR, 2.7.5 hasn't shipped)

- **`entryExists` swallowed every `lstat` error**, so a component that exists but can't be inspected (EACCES, ELOOP) read as absent and the walk stepped past it. Only ENOENT/ENOTDIR may report absent now; everything else fails closed.
- **The segment boundary had no test.** Replacing it with a bare `startsWith` left all 19 tests green while admitting `/Volumes-evil`, `/private/tmp-evil` and a sibling of the home root.

  Worth recording so it isn't "simplified" back: the *obvious* test proves nothing. Asserting that `/Volumes-evil/x.png` is refused passes even with the boundary broken, because that path doesn't exist, so its deepest existing ancestor is `/` — which is in no allowed root, and it's rejected for an unrelated reason. The real test injects a root set and creates an actual prefix-sharing sibling directory.

## Verification

Every guard was proven by breaking it:

| Reverted | Result |
|---|---|
| the whole symlink fix | **4 tests fail** — including one that fails on the *side effect*: `mkdir -p` had genuinely created a directory outside every allowed root |
| segment boundary → bare `startsWith` | **1 test fails** (was 0 — completely unguarded) |

Two tests are anti-vacuity controls that pass in **both** states, proving the fix doesn't just refuse everything: a symlink that stays inside the roots is still accepted, and so are the real `/private/...` spellings behind `/tmp` and `/var/folders`.

Full suite 583 passing; typecheck, lint, format clean; bundle rebuilt and committed (`git status` empty after a re-run). 2.7.5 with a real CHANGELOG heading.

## One judgment call to confirm

A destination that already exists as a symlink is refused **even when its target is inside an allowed root** — so `~/latest.png -> ~/Pictures/x.png` is now refused. apple-mail-mcp refuses *all* pre-existing destinations, so this is strictly looser than mail; I kept notes' existing overwrite-a-regular-file behaviour and closed only the symlink case. Say if you'd rather match mail exactly.

## Summary & Motivation (Problem vs. Solution)

Ports the [cross-origin hardening](https://github.com/tkhq/frames/pull/129) to the auth frame

Two fixes:

**Any window could open the MessageChannel.** The `TURNKEY_INIT_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` handler only checked for `event.ports?.[0]`. It now also requires `event.source === window.parent`, a real (non-`"null"`) origin, and exactly one port.

**The embedded key was shared across embedders.** One P-256 key lived in localStorage under `TURNKEY_EMBEDDED_KEY`, created at DOMContentLoaded before we knew the parent, so every embedder got the same `PUBLIC_KEY_READY` and an auth bundle could be replayed from any origin. Keys are now per-origin: `TURNKEY_EMBEDDED_KEY_V2:<encodeURIComponent(origin)>`, bound at the handshake. Legacy iframe-stamper (< 2.1.0) clients get an in-memory-only key until a real origin shows up, and the old `TURNKEY_EMBEDDED_KEY` is purged rather than migrated. Binding to a second origin is rejected; a failed handshake rolls back to ephemeral.

## Tests

`auth/index.test.js`, 34 passing. Covers per-origin key isolation, second-origin rejection, invalid origins, legacy purge, ephemeral-stays-in-memory, and the five channel-gate rejection cases.

## Reference to Linear Issue (ENG-XXX)

[ENG-4596](https://linear.app/turnkey/issue/ENG-4596) / TKA-20260806-016. Siblings: #129 (export-and-sign), #130 (import).

## What changed

Nine call sites across five modules (`feedback_store.py:521`, `run_history_store.py:416`, `feedback_audit.py:685/691/995`, `store_reconnect.py:325/366`, `query_runs.py:2358/2492`) log a raw exception via `%s`, which calls `str(exc)` with no scrubbing before it reaches `JsonFormatter`. Verified (2026-08-13/14): the exception types actually caught there — `sqlite3.Error`, `TimeoutError`, JSON parse errors, one `HTTPError`/`URLError` pair — don't currently stringify to include a credential, so this is a latent gap, not a live leak. But nothing enforced that property, and a future call site reusing one of those `except` blocks for something that does carry a secret would leak it with no filter to catch it.

`src/product_app/logging_config.py`'s `JsonFormatter` runs `_redact_secrets` against the fully-rendered JSON log line before it's emitted, scrubbing:
- `Bearer <token>` (the shape of an `Authorization` header value)
- labeled credential assignments (`api_key=...`, `access_token: ...`, `password=...`, etc.), bare **or quoted** on either side of the separator (`password="hunter2"`, `'password': 'hunter2'`)
- bare key-shaped tokens (`sk-...`, `AKIA...`)

`install_redaction_record_factory()` additionally redacts at `LogRecord` creation time — both the interpolated message (via a `setLogRecordFactory` hook) and any string-valued `extra={...}` field (via a `Logger.makeRecord` wrapper, since extras are attached by `makeRecord` *after* the record factory runs and are otherwise invisible to it). This closes the Sentry breadcrumb/event bypass: `sentry_sdk`'s `LoggingIntegration` reads records via a patched `callHandlers`, never through `JsonFormatter`, so the stdout-only scrub in the original version of this PR left Sentry unprotected. `synthesis.py:1462` (`logger.error("synthesis_section_failed", extra={"error": str(exc), ...})`) is a real, existing call site that logs through `extra`, not a hypothetical one.

Three ADRs record the decisions: `docs/adr/0040-global-log-redaction-filter-over-per-call-site-fixes.md` (the original decision to build a global filter over auditing 9 call sites), `docs/adr/0041-record-factory-redaction-closes-the-sentry-bypass.md` (redact at record-creation time, not only in `JsonFormatter`), and `docs/adr/0042-module-level-idempotency-flag-for-chained-record-factories.md` (idempotency tracked by a module flag, not a marker on the current factory — closes a chain-growth and reentrancy bug). Numbered 0040-0042, not 0036-0038, to avoid colliding with ADR-0036-0039 added by #303/#143/#167/#145/#160 after this branch was cut.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/test_logging_config_redaction.py` — positive controls (Bearer token, `sk-...` key, `key=value`, `key="value"`, and `'key': 'value'` assignments scrubbed in both a plain message and a real logged exception) and negative controls (an ordinary message and a real non-secret exception survive untouched). Each new test states what turns it red; confirmed by mutation (copy-aside/restore, never `git checkout`).
- `tests/unit/test_logging_config_sentry_redaction.py` — drives a real `sentry_sdk` client with an in-memory `before_breadcrumb` hook (not a mock) to prove a Bearer token, a bare `sk-...` key, and a secret passed via `extra={...}` never reach a Sentry breadcrumb in plaintext, plus positive partners proving non-secret messages/extras survive untouched, the reentrancy guard doesn't disable redaction, and repeated `setup_json_logging()` calls don't grow the factory chain.
- The quoted-value regex had a real near-miss during review: an initial fix using two independent optional quotes (`["']?` on each side) corrupted `JsonFormatter`'s JSON output by eating the JSON string's own structural closing quote whenever the credential value was unquoted and sat at the message's end (`api_key=abcdef...` immediately before `"`) — caught by the existing `test_key_value_assignment_secret_is_redacted` going from green to a `JSONDecodeError`. Fixed by requiring every opening quote to be closed by the *same* quote type via a backreference, so an unquoted value never has a trailing quote consumed at all.

## Gates run locally

- `make quality` — 2913 passed, 55 skipped, 95.18% coverage
- `make validate` — all gates passed, ADR index up to date (**42** records)
- `make diff-cover DIFF_BASE=origin/main` — `logging_config.py` 100% (49/49 changed lines)
- `make api-contract` — 51 passed
- `make openapi-check` — passed
- `make security-scan` — 0 findings (1085 files scanned)

…, missing controls

Closes a coverage gap against njsscan, an established Node scanner: of 78 existing rules only ~20 were JavaScript, and template files were not read at all. Adds three pieces, plus a guard fix that was silently suppressing rules.

packages/scan/src/node-rules.ts — 25 Node-ecosystem rules, each of which has to know which package it is looking at before it can claim anything: vm/vm2 execution, function-reconstructing deserialisers, server-side template injection, shelljs, $where and XPath assembly, XML entity resolution, the JWT `none` algorithm, broken/ECB/legacy ciphers, autoescape and serialize-javascript opt-outs, reflected CORS origins, headless-browser navigation, zip-slip, Electron renderer settings, disabled security headers, buffer bounds and uninitialised allocation, oversized body limits, and returned stack traces.

packages/scan/src/template-rules.ts — a second engine keyed on file extension rather than language, because the extension is what names the template engine and the engine is what decides which syntax skips escaping. Covers Handlebars/ Mustache, Vue, Pug/Jade, EJS/ECT, Dust, Nunjucks/Twig/Jinja and Haml. Runs alongside the code rules, so a .vue file is still checked as JavaScript.

packages/scan/src/controls.ts — reports controls the tree has no evidence of (headers, CSRF, rate limiting, body size limits). Whole-project, so it accumulates across the walk; opt-in behind `threatcrush scan --missing-controls` because an absence is a weaker claim than a present defect; and silent unless the tree actually serves HTTP.

Guard fix in code-rules.ts. GENERIC_GUARD is case-insensitive, so the "Allow" in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` matched its allow-list heuristic. As the guard is tested against an 8-line window, one CORS header line disabled every guardable rule around it — in the end-to-end fixture it suppressed both the `none`-algorithm finding and a returned stack trace. The failure mode was the dangerous kind: not fewer findings, none, indistinguishable from clean code. Scoped to the header prefix so real allow-lists, including `allow-list:` keys in scanned config files, keep guarding. Covered by a regression test.

Written clean-room. njsscan is LGPL-3.0 and this package is MIT, so its rule definitions could not be reused even in translation; only the list of vulnerability classes was taken, which is a fact about the ecosystem rather than an expression of it. Every pattern, guard and message is original and written against this engine's confidence model, which njsscan does not share. Provenance and the licence reasoning are recorded in the module headers, and classes needing analysis this engine does not do are listed in KNOWN_GAPS rather than approximated.

Tests: 252 pass in packages/scan (58 new), 2 in apps/cli; both packages typecheck; CLI builds; verified end to end against a fixture app.

## Importer

`npm run feed:import` fetched 1,842 advisories over 19 pages and mapped 4,782 IOCs, of which 4,549 were already in the feed and 64 already covered by a bare-name entry. **169 new entries written, 122 corroborated against OSV.dev.** All npm.

Nothing was reported unmappable, no page cap was hit, and nothing was left waiting behind `--limit` (169 is under the 250 default), so the next run starts from a clean window.

### False-positive review

59 of the 169 are bare names rather than version pins, which is the shape that would hurt if one of them were an established package. As a first pass, twelve of the riskiest-looking (`react-shield`, `source-analyzer`, `root-locator`, `path-match-js`, `ts-enum-helper`, `mutex-forge`, `sourceflow-tracker`, `finvu-hdfc-sdk`, `blocks-angular`, `index-design-system`, `lab-helper`, `nolimit-agent`) were each created 2026-08-13 with a single published version. `nolimit-agent` is the outlier worth noting: 12,272 downloads in 30 days off a one-day-old single-version package.

Partial on #4842 and #5081 — see below. Both remain open with the residue named.

## #6444 — a default install reached a third party on recall

`AcademicSource` was registered **unconditionally**. `available()` returned `true` unconditionally. A missing API key produced a warning and nothing else.

So the actual trust boundary was **registration**, not the key — and nothing gated it. Adds `recall_sources.academic.enabled`, defaulting `false`.

The test asserts a default `AletheiaConfig` registers **exactly one** source (the local `llm_context`). Against the old path that count is two, so it fails without the fix. That satisfies the issue's "deny-all network test" at the *registration* boundary rather than the transport one — no HTTP mocking needed, because the source is never constructed.

`memory_search`'s tool description now discloses that it is local-only unless a source is explicitly enabled, and `docs/NETWORK.md` gains the `api.semanticscholar.org` row.

## #4842 — external tools bypassed the SSRF guard entirely (partial)

`ExternalToolExecutor` built its own bare `reqwest::Client` and called `.send()` directly: no `EgressGate`, no private-IP check, no redirect revalidation, no response cap. `organon`'s `http_client` had all four, from SECURITY #5071 and #5229.

**Rather than copy that machinery**, the pieces aletheia needed became `pub` and external tools now call them — one implementation, two callers, which is the issue's own stated preference.

One consequence worth flagging for review: the client is now built with `.redirect(Policy::none())`. `send_with_safe_redirects` follows redirects **manually** so it can revalidate each hop; a client that also auto-followed would silently skip its own revalidation.

Tests use RFC 5737 and link-local literals, so no DNS or network is involved. `refuses_private_endpoint_without_connecting` points at `169.254.169.254` and asserts refusal *before* any connection — deterministic, unlike "connection failed", which the old code also produced but for the wrong reason and depending on what happened to be listening.

> **Correction.** This section originally said stdio MCP servers need subprocess sandboxing. **They are already sandboxed** — `organon::sandbox::apply_sandbox` with Landlock + seccomp, a cwd-scoped write root, and `env_clear()`, landed via `6261ffd58` before this PR was opened, with four tests asserting it. I asserted a gap without checking the tree. The streamable-HTTP transport half was real and is fixed in #6776.

**Deliberately not taken:** MCP server registration — stdio subprocess spawn and the streamable-HTTP transport in `diaporeia`. That needs subprocess sandboxing or an explicit local-trust declaration, the same URL/redirect validation on a transport that currently has none, and trust metadata surfaced in manifests. That is a second crate's transport layer plus a schema addition; doing it rushed alongside these would have been worse than leaving it named.

## #5081 — most of it was already fixed (partial)

Verified against the tree rather than assumed. Already done: `allowed_root` no longer defaults to `~`; the non-Linux `nproc_limit` and process-group-kill gaps are `cfg`-handled with a `SECURITY(#5237)` note, not silent; `SandboxGuarantees`/`probe_guarantees` exist with tests; `validate()` already hard-refuses an unenforceable allowlist under `enforcing`.

**Two gaps genuinely survived:**

1. `validate()` flagged permissive enforcement, a broad `allowed_root`, and a non-loopback allowlist — but **never `egress = "allow"`**, which is the compiled default and the widest-open of the four. An operator reading its output saw three of four.
2. **`check-config` never called `validate()` at all.** It checks `gateway.auth.mode` explicitly but had no sandbox equivalent, despite `register_domain_tools` using exactly that mechanism at startup.

Now it does — and a config the server would *refuse to boot* reports `[FAIL]`, not `[warn]`. `check-config` must not print "Configuration OK" for a config that cannot start.

snapshot_payload.body:
## What problem does this solve?

First implementation slice (PR 1 of 4) of the Agent Control Plane ADR (#1465): the standalone `openab-cp` binary — wire protocol, identity-bound registry, CP-authoritative policy engine, and delegation router. Agents delegate to each other over ACP/WS instead of round-tripping through Discord/Telegram.

Planned follow-up PRs: (2) OAB-side `[control_plane]` config + registration client + worker pool wiring, (3) MCP facade over UDS + `openab agent <verb>` CLI, (4) streaming + observer endpoint.

## What's in this PR

- **`crates/openab-cp`** (new workspace member, standalone binary per the `openab-gateway` precedent):
  - `proto.rs` — versioned JSON-RPC 2.0 envelopes; `cp/register`(+ack), `cp/heartbeat`, `cp/delegate`, `cp/delegate_result`, `cp/cancel`; distinct machine-actionable error codes (`IDENTITY_MISMATCH`, `POLICY_DENIED`, `NO_TARGET`, `SATURATED`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `TARGET_DISCONNECTED`, `DUPLICATE_DELEGATION`, `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`)
  - `config.rs` — CP-owned identity table (auth key → immutable `namespace`/`name`/`type` claims, `${ENV_VAR}` expansion, constant-time key lookup, duplicate-key rejection), per-namespace policy overrides
  - `registry.rs` — instance registry with replica semantics (rolling deploys route new work to the newest healthy instance), lease/heartbeat expiry, saturation-aware selection distinguishing `NO_TARGET` from `SATURATED`
  - `policy.rs` — CP-authoritative checks: initiator role, depth, cycle (incl. self), namespace boundary, deadline sanity/cap/parent-budget
  - `router.rs` — in-flight table; **CP-constructed chain** (callers pass only `parent_delegation_id`; ancestry derives from authenticated identities — unforgeable); deadline sweep (synthesized `timeout` + best-effort `cp/cancel`); disconnect handling both directions; result size truncation; idempotency
  - `server.rs` — axum WS server; auth via `Authorization: Bearer` at upgrade (keys never in URLs); mandatory `cp/register` first frame verified against the key's bound identity
- **ADR amendments** (`docs/adr/agent-control-plane.md`): new "v1 contract amendments" section freezing the #1465 review findings (identity binding, CP-authoritative policy, restart/saturation/timeout semantics, result cap, idempotency); §11 Q1 streaming resolved as committed fast-follow with the observer endpoint sketch.

## Review Contract

### Goal
Ship a correct, tested control-plane core (registry + router + policy + wire contract) that later PRs (runtime client, facade, streaming) build on without protocol changes, implementing the frozen ADR baseline including the #1465 review checklist items.

### Non-goals
No OAB-runtime-side code: no `[control_plane]` config section, no registration client, no MCP facade/UDS/CLI, no streaming/observer endpoint (PRs 2–4). No CP HA (single instance; restart semantics are defined and implemented). No durable state, queueing, or delegation history. No Docker/Helm packaging.

### Accepted Residual Risks
- Wire contract is exercised by unit tests, not yet by a real OAB runtime client; PR 2 integration may surface adjustments. Mitigation: `protocol_version` field + `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` rejection gives a compatibility gate.
- Registered-runtime JSON-RPC responses to CP-forwarded frames are logged and dropped (correlation is by `delegation_id`, not rpc id). Acceptable for v1; revisit if per-frame acks become necessary.
- `cp/cancel` to a serving runtime is best-effort; a runtime that ignores it burns tokens until its own deadline handling stops it. The propagated deadline is the hard upper bound.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Registration rejects: wrong first frame, unsupported protocol version, identity claim mismatch (namespace/name/type each), empty instance_id — all tested
- Policy denies: worker initiation (default), depth > namespace max, cycles incl. self-delegation, cross-namespace, past/over-cap/over-parent deadlines — all tested
- Router: happy-path roundtrip with CP-stamped chain; duplicate id rejection; saturation fast-fail; deadline sweep synthesizing timeout+cancel; worker/initiator disconnect handling; spoofed-completion rejection; late-result drop (CP restart case); oversized-result truncation — all tested
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p openab-cp` (42/42), `cargo check --workspace` all pass
- No mockall, no network/fs in unit tests, tests inline `#[cfg(test)]`

### Follow-ups
- PR 2: `[control_plane]` OAB config + outbound registration client (gateway.rs backoff shape) + worker pool wiring
- PR 3: MCP facade (`spawn_agent`, `check_delegation`, `list_agents`, `cancel_delegation`) over UDS + CLI
- PR 4: streaming frames + read-only `/observe` endpoint + `openab-cp tail`
- Packaging (Dockerfile/Helm) once PR 2 makes the binary deployable end-to-end

## Verified

On macmini at the squashed head (content-identical to ac9c023):
- `cargo fmt -p openab-cp -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p openab-cp --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p openab-cp` — 42 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo check --workspace` — passes with the new member

## ⚠️ Breaking Change — `admission` is required on `cp/delegate_result` and `cp/cancel`

The CP wire protocol gains a required `admission` token on two frames:
`cp/delegate_result` (round-8 revision) and `cp/cancel` (this revision, both
directions). Both are **required** fields, so this is a wire-breaking protocol
change: a runtime built against the pre-token contract has **every** result and
**every** cancel refused with `INVALID_PARAMS` once the CP is upgraded.

There is no backward-compatible spelling. An optional token would mean "apply
this frame to whatever holds the `delegation_id` right now", which is precisely
the misdelivery the token exists to close: `delegation_id` is client-supplied
and cancel-then-retry legitimately reuses it, so with a single replica the retry
re-admits the same id to the same worker. Without a token on the wire, a late
result for the cancelled admission is delivered to the initiator as the retry's
terminal frame and commits the retry — releasing capacity it still occupies —
and a stale or CP-synthesized cancel for the ended admission aborts the retry's
work at the worker.

### Migration for runtime authors

- **Serving runtimes:** copy `admission` from the forwarded `cp/delegate` into
  the matching `cp/delegate_result`. Match incoming `cp/cancel` on the token,
  not on `delegation_id`: a CP-synthesized cancel names the admission it ends
  and can arrive *after* a forward that reused the same id.
- **Initiators:** read `admission` from the `cp/delegate` ack. Send it on
  `cp/cancel` to name the admission you mean to abort — a cancel naming a
  superseded admission is refused, which is what prevents a retried cancel from
  killing the re-admission that replaced its target. Correlate terminal frames
  on `admission`, not on `delegation_id` ("first terminal frame per admission
  wins").
- **Refusals are indistinguishable by design.** An unknown id, another
  instance's live id, and your own id under a superseded admission all return
  the same byte-identical `POLICY_DENIED`. Treat a refusal as "not mine / not
  live" and reconcile against your own state; the CP deliberately reports
  nothing about whether an id is currently re-admitted.

No shipped clients are affected at this point in the stack — every serving
runtime in PRs 2–4 learns the token from the forwarded `cp/delegate` — so the
migration is mechanical. It is not, however, silent or optional.

Contract details: `docs/adr/agent-control-plane.md` §4 (v1 contract
amendments, "Admissions carry a protocol-visible token"); runtime-author
summary in `docs/control-plane.md` ("Client behavior to expect").
